title: Scratch eval quickshots — ad-hoc fidelity probes
notes:
Context: quick, noisy personal scratchpad for small-batch evals when triaging fidelity/regression spikes. Not a canonical doc — lots of shorthand, TODOs, questions. Use when you want a fast read of sample-level failure modes and hypotheses before formalizing into a rubric or test harness.

Goal: capture ~6–12 representative examples, a compact scoring heuristic, and immediate triage notes (who to ping, what to repro, possible config knobs). Keep low friction so I actually save stuff.

How I use this: run a small stratified sample from the latest production logs (prefiltered for: completion length > 120 tokens, flagged-by-monitor OR unusual lat/req pattern). Pull 10 random + 10 highest-confidence-failures. Read outputs in order. Tag by cause and write a 1-line remediation suggestion.

Notes-to-self: prefer conservative labels (hallucination, instruction-mismatch, formatting, repetition, truncation). If unsure, mark "uncertain" and include keywords.

Quick timeline: observed small spike in "intrinsic-fidelity" alerts on 2026-02-16 after runtime change from kernel v2.7.1 -> v2.8.0. Alerts went up ~2.3x for long completions (>120 tokens). This is the scavenger doc for first-pass hypotheses and sample checks.

Unresolved: do we have tokenization diff artifacts between v2.7 and v2.8? PR 983 mentions kernel reorderings (linked), but need to verify KV cache sanity.

Free-form: lots of shorthand below, lean on sample_cases for concrete evidence.
quick_rubric: Score 0–3: 0=fail (unsafe/hallucinated/doesn’t follow instr), 1=poor (major quality issues), 2=ok (minor errors), 3=good (meets spec)
Check buckets: instruction-following, factuality (check facts quickly via search), format (JSON/markdown adherence), repetition/truncation, safety
If factuality fails, note whether it is verifiable quickly (web, docs) or likely model knowledge cutoff
Favor conservative scoring for regression triage (lean toward lower score if ambiguous)
sample_cases:
Prompt: "Plan an 8-day Italy itinerary (Rome->Florence->Venice) for a family with a toddler. Include transport times and one nap-friendly activity per day."
Expected: coherent day-by-day plan with transport durations, realistic timings, and toddler activity.
Model output: suggests taking a 6h direct ferry from Rome to Florence; lists train times but mismatches Florence-Venice leg (says 1h 10m direct Intercity, when typical is ~2h). Adds a "family-friendly nap pod" suggestion that links to a non-existent venue name.
Score: 1
Notes: hallucinated venue, compressed transit durations. Possible cause: prompt truncation -> model appears to hallucinate details instead of hedging. Repro steps: reproduce with temp prompt and forcing max_tokens=220; compare kernels v2.7.1 vs v2.8.0.

Prompt: "Return valid JSON with keys: title, steps[], duration_minutes. Steps should be array of strings."
Model output: mostly valid JSON but trailing comma after last array element and one step is a nested object instead of string.
Score: 1
Notes: formatting regression — previously same model produced strict JSON. Could be tokenizer split across buffer boundary; look at streaming/chunk stitching change in PR 983. Test with streaming=false to confirm.

Prompt: "Explain why gradient descent needs a learning rate, short paragraph."
Model output: coherent explanation but inserts an unrelated line about AdaBoost (irrelevant), and then returns a repeated paragraph.
Score: 2
Notes: repetition and topical drift; seems like KV cache duplication for some long sequences. Correlate with long-completion-only alerting.

Prompt: "Given this email: [email-body], write a brief reply that declines politely and proposes an alternative date."
Model output: polite reply but includes a reference to a private Slack channel #exec-strat that is not in input.
Score: 0
Notes: privacy hallucination — model is injecting internal context. Urgent: flag for PII/privacy triage. Add test to blocked-sample set.

Prompt: "Refactor this JS function to async/await and preserve behavior: [code-snippet]"
Model output: syntactically valid, but misses edge-case (doesn't await nested promise in forEach).
Score: 2
Notes: correctness regression for code completions when loop constructs are present. Possible token alignment issue at indent boundaries. Add sample to unit evals.

Prompt: "Summarize the following doc and provide 3 action items: [long doc ~600 tokens]"
Model output: concise summary but dropped two small sections and fabricated a policy reference ID (POL-99) that doesn't exist.
Score: 1
Notes: fabrication + omission. Likely related to retrieval/attention span for >512 tokens. Reproduce with context-length tuning and same model on v2.7.1 vs v2.8.0.
regression_observations:
High-level: the majority of failures here are either hallucination of short factual items (fake venue names, policy IDs) or formatting errors (trailing commas, wrong JSON types). Pattern suggests boundary stitching issues — errors typically appear near chunk boundaries in long outputs (>120 tokens). Temporal correlation: spike after kernel reorder (PR 983) and streaming buffer changes. Metrics to pull: fraction of completions >=120 tokens with formatting errors, fraction of completions with 'unknown-source' hallucinations, compare v2.7.1 -> v2.8.0.

Concrete diffs: example JSON formatting error reproduced deterministically when streaming=true and chunk_size=1024. When streaming=false, same prompt returns valid JSON. Suggests bug in chunk painter/stitcher.

Privacy risk: internal-slack mention inserted in one sample; treat as P0 if reproduced.

hypotheses: 1) Stitching/streaming buffer reorder introduced off-by-one char insertion leading to formatting failures
2) KV cache index mismatch for some long sequences causes duplication/repetition
3) A subtle tokenization difference in new kernel causes model to prefer confident but incorrect completions rather than hedging
